Subject: Re: Sizing info - private vs dedicated question

Hi Anna,

Thanks for the sync earlier. Per our conversation, I put together a quick worksheet to help compare two onramp paths for CardioGuard: (A) Dedicated-reserved GPUs for the whole workload, and (B) a hybrid where PHI-bound traffic is routed to Private (VPC/air-gapped) nodes while the rest lands on Dedicated.

Attached: CG_onramp_sizing.xlsx — low-level assumptions are on tab "input". Key asks from you to make the numbers concrete:
- Expected peak concurrent requests (p50/p95) and typical batchability (are requests batched on client side?)
- Average and 95th percentile sequence lengths (tokens) for inference
- Whether any training / fine-tuning will run on the same fleet (impacts GPU reservation)

Initial notes from our side: we can support an initial hybrid pilot with the following high-level footprint: 4x A100-80GB-equivalent for Private (PHI-only), 8x A100-80GB equivalent in Dedicated with burst pool for seasonality. This gives a predictable baseline and an escape hatch to Dedicated for non-PHI traffic.

Can you confirm the p95 latency SLO you need and procurement timeline? If procurement wants a single-option price we can produce both route-level and blended estimates.

Thanks — I'll loop Marissa for the detailed cost sketch once we have the p95 and seq lengths.

—Naomi

- Sequence lengths: median ~120 tokens, 95th ~520 tokens.

Procurement note: they asked for a Private-only option pricing as a show-stopper and a Dedicated-only option for comparison. We'd prefer a hybrid as you suggested if that keeps costs predictable and keeps the PHI lane compliant.

Anna / team — looping in engineering to convert those inputs into a practical onramp. High level recommendation (concise):

Option H (Hybrid onramp, recommended):
- Pilot (4 weeks): 2x Private nodes (A100-80GB equiv) sized for PHI lane (22% traffic), 4x Dedicated nodes for non-PHI baseline. Private nodes use strict KMS + VPC peering; Dedicated runs in our Dedicated pool with tenant isolation.
- Canary / scale (4–8 weeks): add 2x Dedicated nodes as buffer and enable autoscale burst to 12x Dedicated for daytime spikes.
- Full onboarding (Q1 ramp): 4x Private + 8x Dedicated reserved (commit), with a 20% burst pool reserved for peak.

Why hybrid: cost-effective because only PHI traffic pays Private premium; predictable latency by reserving Dedicated baseline for non-PHI. Escape hatches: if Private provisioning is delayed, we can temporarily route PHI-like sessions to Dedicated with stricter logging and customer-approved contracts (temporary exception — legal sign-off required).

Estimated one-time onboarding/engineering runbook + compliance evidence: ~2.5 FTE-weeks (Redwood SE time) — cost captured in attached onramp_estimate_v1.pdf. SLA nuance: Private comes with additional audit log retention & customer-managed KMS fees.

Action items
- Naomi / Anna: decide pilot start date (we recommend week of 2026-12-27 to meet procurement cutoff).
- Procurement: confirm if CardioGuard needs Private-only PO or if hybrid pricing is acceptable.
- Engineering (Karthik): finalize kernel/quantization profile for the 520-token tail to hit p95 latency.

If these align I can convert the estimate into a two-option procurement packet (Private-only vs Hybrid blended) for your finance team.

Quick technical checklist based on Marissa's proposal and Anna's traffic profile:

- KV cache fragmentation: with 520-token tails, we recommend quantization-friendly model variant + 1.5x cache memory headroom on Private nodes to avoid mid-session cache churn.
- Kernel selection: use the fused attention kernels for the p50 path and fallback to the memory-optimized kernels for p95; this preserves tail latency. See brief notes attached.
- Routing policy: implement policy-based routing at the inference gateway: PHI flag -> Private; else -> Dedicated. For temporary fallback (if Private unavailable), route to Dedicated with enforced logging and rate-limited concurrency per customer agreement.
- Autoscale tuning: keep lower latency SLOs by pre-warming 1 warm replica per Private node. This avoids cold-starts on the PHI lane.

I added a short text file with kernel/ops notes. I'll follow up with cost-to-perf tradeoffs if we want smaller instances with more aggressive batching.

Karthik
